title: Electromagnets & relays
examples: How does changing the battery affect the magnet's power?
Can you show me an example of a relay in a house?

explain.say: Today we are learning about electromagnets and relays. These are cool uses of electricity and magnets.
The first factor affecting strength is the current flowing through the coil. More current means a stronger magnet.
The second factor is the number of coils wrapped around the core. More coils help make the electromagnet much stronger.
The third factor is the core material. Using a soft iron core concentrates the magnetic field effectively.
Relays use electromagnets to switch a larger circuit. They allow a small current to control a big one.
In everyday life, your home's security alarm uses relays. A small sensor current triggers a large siren sound.

faq.q: Does the magnet only work when electricity is on?
faq.a: Yes, an electromagnet only creates a magnetic field when electric current flows through it. When the current stops, the magnetism disappears.

faq.q: What is the difference between a permanent and an electromagnet?
faq.a: A permanent magnet has its magnetism always, while an electromagnet needs electricity to work. You can turn its magnetism on and off.

faq.q: Why do we use relays in big machines?
faq.a: Relays let us use a small, safe current to switch a much larger, more powerful current. This protects the control circuit.
asks: What is the purpose of a relay?

faq.q: Does the core material really matter for strength?
faq.a: Yes, soft iron is preferred because it magnetises easily and loses its magnetism quickly when the power goes off. This is very useful.

faq.q: What is the basic principle of an electromagnet?
faq.a: The principle is that electricity flowing through a coil of wire creates a magnetic field around it. This is the core idea.

facts: Electromagnets require an electric current to function.
Increasing the current increases the magnetic field strength.
Relays use electromagnets to switch high-power circuits.
Soft iron is often used as the core material.

quiz.say: To make an electromagnet stronger, you should:

options.show: Increase the current or the number of coils.
options.say: Increase the current or the number of coils.

quiz.why: Both increasing the current and increasing the number of coils directly increase the strength of the magnetic field.

wrong.1: Steel cores are too hard and will retain magnetism even when the power is off.
wrong.2: Decreasing the voltage will lower the current and make the magnet weaker.
wrong.3: Fewer coils mean less magnetic field generated overall.

quiz.say: What component allows a small current to control a large one?
quiz.show: Small control signal to big load
quiz.why: The relay acts as an electrically operated switch, using a small input signal to activate a much larger circuit.

wrong.0: An electromagnet is the part that activates the relay, not the whole switching device.
wrong.2: A simple switch requires a person's hand to operate it manually.
wrong.3: The battery only provides the energy source, not the switching mechanism itself.

quiz.say: If you want to switch a very bright light bulb on and off using a low-power battery, you should use:
quiz.show: Low power control, high power load
quiz.why: The relay safely isolates the low-power control circuit from the high-power load circuit.

wrong.0: Direct wiring would require the low-power battery to supply enough energy for the bright bulb.
wrong.1: A simple switch cannot handle the high current needed for the bright bulb safely.
wrong.2: Permanent magnets cannot be turned off or controlled by an external electrical signal.
